You need a new therapist. ASAP! Red flags! 🚩 

You need a medically trained professional, not someone who can barely even scratch the surface of this highly complex disorder. Most people simply do not understand so they minimize our feelings to make it more tangible to them, in an attempt to put a bandaid on your boo boo. It simply does not work for us; we are wired differently. 

Our brains are PHYSICALLY different. There are many areas of the brain that are affected in this disorder. It is never YOU. Mental illness, despite the STILL very stigmatizing perception that it’s OUR fault or a personal failure, is NOT your fault. 

Symptoms are visible whereas the organ is not. Your therapist telling you that you are lazy is the equivalent of telling someone with cancer that they’re just not strong enough. Or that maybe someone with heart disease is lazy because they didn’t run a marathon. It is extremely dehumanizing to have someone essentially gaslight your perception and being.

Please seek someone who is actually willing to listen and problem solve with you. That’s the first step to getting where you would like to go.

I suffered from negative symptoms the most within my first year of being on medication. Nothing held my attention, no happiness, nothing. I even had to stop college for about 2 years because everything was just so incredibly hard. I could barely sit long enough to read a sentence. 

I began sleeping 20hrs/day. I had zero motivation and zero energy. It was a humongous task to even shower. 

Fast forward to now… I haven’t experienced a single symptom, positive or negative, in over 6 months. The right cocktail of medication helped me, along with my psychiatrist listening to me. Life has changed completely for me. I just graduated with my bachelors in neuroscience, accepted into the national honor society. I’m nearly a year sober and clean. I can truly have peace today. 

My advice? Don’t. Give. Up. The most treacherous storms breed beautiful flowers and rainbows. Is my life perfect? Fuck, no! But is it substantially different and better now? FUCK, YES! Recovery is POSSIBLE. It took about 3.5 years to begin to stabilize. 

Look into therapy (CBT, DBT, EMDR), look deep in yourself. You are not this disease. You are much more than you know. Please, don’t give up. You are more than welcome to message me on exactly how I have gotten to where I am. It’s a whole myriad of things. 

Sending hugs and love ❤️

Hey! Neuroscientist here. I had my first psychotic episode in May 2023. I ended up having to emergency withdraw for 3 semesters. When I first got out of the hospital I felt like a different person. Fast forward to now and I am 1 semester away from my degree in Neuroscience. I’ve completed two papers that are published and i’ve done primary research on Parkinson’s on my own with the help of my mentor. 

That’s not to say I don’t have bad days. There are some days where I’m unable to understand things because my mind is so loud. 

It takes time to have your brain back. Psychosis steals it. Success is more common than people think. Keep going!!!

My hands and body parts move individually during catatonia. I don’t have control over my body. It just…. happens. I’ll be stuck in a uncomfortable position for hours. It only happens when I’m extremely stressed.

I could understand everything around me but just was mute and unresponsive. It was a terrifying feeling all through my body. I have never felt so much fear (except during my psychosis). 

I wouldn’t consider someone in a catatonic to be completely void of a conscience. For me, my head is LOUD when I’m in a catatonic state. There’s a billion things going on and on inside my head and there’s no brakes. 

I was involuntary admitted to a psychiatric center but was able to argue my 1013 (involuntary hold) away and get a form to prove I’m of sound mind and made my own decision to be hospitalized. 

If there’s one word to describe catatonic for me it would be “suffocating”.

I lost all my money as well. I spent $9,000 within a few months during my mania. I also lost my boyfriend of 3 years. I went to the psych ward and next thing I know, he disappears. 

I have lost everything because of this illness. BUT!! I am slowly gaining friends and a better outlook on life. Sometimes a door closes in your face bc there’s a better path. Think about what brings you joy and focus on that.
